summary: Norfolk, CT lookout station from about 1911 on Dennis Hill; register says a replica platform followed a 1992 photo, unconfirmed today. Site is a public state park.

facts.design: Open platform reached by an outside wooden staircase from the octagonal stone summit building (1908 bungalow); the original tower stood atop the Dennis summer home
facts.status_note: Register says a replica was built after a 1992 photo was recovered; no source we read describes it, and a 2014 visitor's page describes only a former deck that burned
facts.agency: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (Dennis Hill State Park)

access.note: Free state park administered by CT DEEP; summit road open late April to early November per a 2014 visitor's page

visit.trail_note: You can hike up at any time (2014 visitor's page)

events.note: Architect Alfredo S.G. Taylor designed the summit bungalow for Dr. Frederick Shepard Dennis
First lookout station on Dennis Hill established by State Forester Samuel Spring, about 1911
Listed as one of four Connecticut lookout towers in operation; Dennis Hill was one (Hartford Current, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Dr. Dennis gave the estate to the state; Wikipedia gives 1935
A photo of the original tower was recovered; the register says a replica platform was built on the site afterward (no date for the replica)
Registered September 9, 2008 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

corrections.why: The register gives only the site elevation (1,640 ft, 500 m). No source we read gives a tower height of 191.1 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1,640 ft (500 m); the 1955 Telegram and the 2014 CTMQ page give 1,627 ft. The 13-foot gap is not resolved; the story gives both figures.
The 1955 Bridgeport Telegram says Dr. Dennis gave the estate in 1934; Wikipedia says 1935. The story reports both.
The register says a replica was built after a 1992 photo. The 2014 CTMQ page describes only the former deck, which burned, and does not mention a replica. Neither source dates the change.

notes_for_editor: Replica status is unverified; no source dates the replica or the pavilion fire, and no source we read describes the summit structure today. Record height_m of 191.1 is unsupported (proposed removal). The 1911 date rests on a state report as quoted by the Forest Lookouts site, not the report itself. The CTMQ page is a 2014 personal visit, so road hours may have changed. A current visit or a recent photo would settle the replica question.
